newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina says Vietnam authorizes meat exports.
newsitem.headline: Argentina says Vietnam authorizes meat exports.

text.p: Vietnam has authorized Argentine meat imports after a sanitary agreement between the two countries, the Argentine government's animal and food sanitation and health service (Senasa) said Wednesday.
Argentina will now be able to export fresh beef and sheep meat, heat-processed meats, hamburgers and chicken, as well as milk and dairy products, Senasa said.
Exports of cattle semen and embryos, breeder cattle and bone meal will also be permitted.
The agreement is the latest in a string of accords which have followed Argentina's victories in the war against foot and mouth disease.
Many Asian countries, like Hong Kong, Singapore, Malaysia and the Philippines, now permit Argentine beef exports, while Indonesia and Thailand are close to opening their markets.

The government hopes Japan and South Korea will follow the lead of the United States, which President Carlos Menem said Tuesday will permit imports of 20,000 tonnes a year after Argentina is officially declared foot-and-mouth free in May.

Argentina exported about 470,000 tonnes of beef in 1996 and the government hopes sales will reach one million tonnes by 2000, even though many in the industry say privately this target is overly optimistic.
